reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that personality mechanisms—repression, fixation, and sign-magic—are foundational cognitive operators that generate higher-order behaviors. Repression and fixation manifest in phobias as persistent, irrational fears without logical basis. These are modeled as deterministic functions of time and environmental triggers. Sign-magic, however, introduces a stochastic element through symbolic reinterpretation, where meaning shifts alter behavior unpredictably. The epistemic structure suggests that while repression and fixation form stable attractors in psychological phase space, sign-magic acts as a perturbation term. This allows for a dual framework: GSI uses Bayesian inference to predict repression/fixation-driven behavior, while GSE employs symbolic dynamics to simulate sign-magic-induced behavioral shifts. Failure modes occur when repression and fixation dominate (leading to rigid pathology) or when sign-magic lacks grounding (leading to delusional behavior).
